requirement:
Source inspection uses the project directory and respects `.gitignore`,
including nested ignore files and their exceptions. Untracked files are
available unless ignored. The same scope applies to listing, reading,
outlining, text search, and structural search, including requests naming a
file or subdirectory directly.

Files outside the project directory and Git metadata are excluded. A direct
read of an excluded file returns an error.
rationale:
I judge the tests adequate for `requirements.sdk.sources.local_provider`. I did not request any implementation source. The assessment rests only on the supplied test text.

**`.gitignore` is respected, including nested files and exceptions.**
- `tests/source_defaults.rs#fn[gitignore_is_shared_by_all_operations_with_or_without_a_git_repository]` builds a root `.gitignore` with `*.txt`, `!keep.txt` and `skip/`. It also adds `src/.gitignore` with `!nested.txt` and `skip/.gitignore` with `!rescue.txt`.
- It asserts that `keep.txt` and `src/nested.txt` are listed. That covers a root exception and a nested exception that overrides an ignore pattern.
- It asserts that `ignored.txt`, `src/ignored.txt` and everything under `skip/` are not listed. This includes `skip/rescue.txt`, whose nested exception must not rescue a file in an ignored directory.
- It runs with and without a Git repository. In the repository case it force-adds `ignored.txt` and still asserts it is excluded.
- A nested ignore file that adds a new ignore pattern, rather than an exception, is not tested on its own. The nested-ignore and exception handling that is tested goes through the same mechanism, and the requirement does not single that case out. I do not treat it as a gap.

**Untracked files are available unless ignored.** `keep.txt` and `.visible` are untracked and are listed. The `src/nested.txt` and `src/ignored.txt` cases are also covered.

**The same scope applies to every operation, including direct requests.**
- Listing: `list(&SourceScope::under(name))` returns an empty result for ignored files and directories. `symlinks_cannot_reopen_ignored_files_or_leave_the_project` and `local_provider_scopes_paths_and_rejects_resources_outside_its_root` cover listing scoped to a subdirectory.
- Reading: `read` is asserted to be an error for `ignored.txt`, `src/ignored.txt` and `skip/rescue.txt`.
- Outlining: `parse` is asserted to be an error for the same ignored paths. `agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[outline_tool_rejects_excluded_and_unreadable_sources_without_domain_reads]` checks the `outline_source` tool. It accepts `source.txt` and rejects ignored files, `../source.txt`, `.git/config`, missing files and a non-string path.
- Text search: `search_text` scoped to the ignored paths returns no matches. A search scoped to `./src/../src` returns only `src/nested.txt`, not `src-old/other.rs`.
- Structural search: `built_in_languages_and_structural_search_use_the_project_scope` shows that `hidden.rs`, `skip` and `.git` return no matches. It also checks that scoping to `visible.rs` works.

**Files outside the project and Git metadata are excluded, and a direct read of an excluded file is an error.**
- `local_provider_scopes_paths_and_rejects_resources_outside_its_root` asserts that listing `..` or an absolute outside path is an error. It also asserts that `read` and `parse_sync` of an absolute outside path are errors.
- On Unix, a symlink to an outside directory and a symlink to an outside file are both rejected. `symlinks_cannot_reopen_ignored_files_or_leave_the_project` also rejects a symlink to an ignored file and a symlink into an outside directory, and it accepts a symlink to a visible file.
- Text search and structural search scoped to `..` are errors.
- `.git/config` read is an error, and `.git` is excluded from listing and from text and structural search.
- `agent/configured.rs#mod[tests]/fn[supplied_agent_uses_attached_project_tools_in_both_configuration_orders]` shows the agent tools see the same scope end to end. `list_sources` omits the ignored file, and `read_source` of the ignored file returns an "excluded" error.

All obligations have tests with assertions that enforce the required outcomes, so I found no adequacy gap.
